own_scenes.desc: Quizá la escuela regional más importante de los noventa salió de la escena más improbable y la que menos discos vendió: el post-rock de Kentucky. Slint y Bitch Magnet (1989) introducen un estilo enrevesado, angular y cerebral, «progresivo para una época que ya no apreciaba las emociones enfáticas»; lo continúan Gastr Del Sol, For Carnation, June Of 44, Rachel's. Chicago lo codifica con acento alemán (Can, Faust, Neu): Tortoise y sus descendientes, Jim O'Rourke (de Cage y Derek Bailey a Fahey y el pop orquestal), DK3, Isotope 217. El rock instrumental (Don Caballero, Godspeed You Black Emperor, Dirty Three, Mogwai, Labradford, Stars Of The Lid); Alemania (Mouse On Mars, To Rococo Rot, Notwist), el «noise-core» japonés (Zeni Geva, Merzbow, Boredoms) y Old Time Relijun, discípulos de Beefheart.

notes.chapter: Cap. 17: Como una autopista: encuentros de electrónica y música popular (1989-2002)
notes.text: Término de Simon Reynolds (1992) para bandas que incorporan tecnología al rock, se alejan de las estructuras lineales y exploran el estudio y la textura; beben del krautrock, la no wave, el post-punk, la electroacústica, el dub y la sampledelia. Su clave: My Bloody Valentine (Glider, Loveless). La «generación perdida» británica: Seefeel, Disco Inferno (D.I. Go Pop), Bark Psychosis (Hex), Insides, Laika, Moonshake, The Third Eye Foundation, desplazada en 1994 por Oasis. Después, el post-rock electrónico alemán (To Rococo Rot, Kreidler, Tarwater) y Radiohead (OK Computer, Kid A).

refs.q: donde más se ha notado la huella de aquellas bandas alemanas de la época ha sido en el post-rock en los noventa
refs.para: El legado de Can ha resistido cualquier tipo de erosión provocada por el paso del tiempo. PiL —su bajista, Jah Wobble, es colaborador habitual de Czukay y Liebezeit—, Brian Eno, Bill Laswell, The Fall, Julián Cope y Thin White Rope son algunos nombres que asumen la deuda contraída, aunque donde más se ha notado la huella de aquellas bandas alemanas de la época ha sido en el post-rock en los noventa: Stereolab, Tortoise, UI y otros grupos actuales como Radiohead parten de rítmica y matices sonoros próximos a Can y, especialmente, a Neu!
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Rock around the click: la electrónica de los setenta, de Hallogallo al ambient en la era del Moog (1968-1982)

refs.q: el término —creado por Simon Reynolds en 1992— era una inteligente manera de explicar y definir el sonido de las bandas
refs.para: El del post-rock es un nombre genérico que arrastra tras de sí el peso de bastantes críticas y prejuicios. Sin embargo, el término —creado por Simon Reynolds en 1992— era una inteligente manera de explicar y definir el sonido de las bandas que por aquel entonces: a) incorporaban a su instrumentación tradicional, basada en el rock, el recurso de las nuevas tecnologías, b) jugaban con o se alejaban de las estructuras lineales, y c) explotaban el uso del estudio y exploraban, a veces de modo profundo, el sonido y los efectos (en algunos casos abandonando la canción a favor de la textura pura). Estas bandas no se nutrían solo de modalidades post-rock previas a 1992 (el célebre krautrock germano, la no wave neoyorquina, el post-punk inglés, anomalías como Cranes, Cocteau Twins o The Young Gods), sino también de la música electroacústica y la concreta, del dub y el reggae, de la sampledelia moderna.
refs.chapter: Cap. 17: Como una autopista: encuentros de electrónica y música popular (1989-2002)

refs.q: Pero lo que impactó realmente a la gran «generación perdida» del pop británico
refs.para: El primer post-rock es ante todo idealismo, un inaudito idealismo. Se trate de las innovaciones del dub, de la remixología o la sampledelia del hip hop, entre otros ejemplos, el post-rock está marcado por la tecnología y sus aplicaciones musicales. Sobre todo, este rock se deja arrastrar por la ciencia del sampler, por su capacidad transformadora; lo fascinante del aparato es su habilidad para reinventar la guitarra, convertir su sonido en nubes, cataratas, tormentas perfectas. Como en Cocteau Twins (los inauditos Cocteau Twins), la guitarra eleva los más etéreos muros de sonido a través de telarañas de samples ambientales, de esas voces lejanas suplicando por no bajar nunca de la nube. Pero lo que impactó realmente a la gran «generación perdida» del pop británico (Seefeel, Disco Inferno, Bark Psychosis, Insides, Laika) fue el rock estratosférico de My Bloody Valentine, y su Glider EP (1990) en particular: una perfecta unión de ruido, belleza y euforia, a un tiempo el sonido más sofisticado del dance —esas guitarras tratadas hasta el punto de parecer beats— y el non plus ultra del rock de gravedad cero. Loveless (1991) supuso la confirmación del visionario talento de Kevin Shields. Free jazz, ambient, noise rock, hip hop, se funden sin ningún prejuicio, epígonos bien avenidos en una disonancia de guitarras etéreas, cataratas de samples y voces cargadas de vértigo: el momento más bello de los noventa y uno de los más grandes de la música de todos los tiempos.

own_scenes.desc: Otra salida para la evolución del techno, mal nombrada: una extensión de las estructuras del rock con apariencia de banda. Míchigan es uno de sus centros (His Name Is Alive, de Livonia, en 4AD; Windy & Carl), aunque apenas ha conectado con el techno de Detroit. Tortoise, formado en Chicago en 1990 por miembros de una docena de bandas y anclado en el batería John McEntire, renunció a guitarras y voces: en directo, vibráfonos, marimbas, guitarras de pedal, sintetizadores y cajas de ritmos para una mezcla de música de baile desenrollada, dub y bandas sonoras, con temas que migran de un proyecto a otro («Jetty», de «La Jetee» de Isotope 217). El indie acabó abrazando la electrónica: Postal Service, Four Tet, Caribou, Broadcast.

influences.name: Industrial, EBM y The Final Cut

refs.q: So we decided: why bother with that?”
refs.para: Post-rock seems to be in a unique position, poised at a nexus of creative possibilities and an understanding of the industry’s ups and downs. Many post-rock bands are more like collectives of adventurous musicians who settle into a groove after a bedouin-like existence of moving from one group to the next. Making the most of this position is Chicago’s Tortoise, formed in 1990 by members of Eleventh Dream Day, Chicago Underground Orchestra, the Poster Children, Bastro, the Tar Babies, and about a dozen others. John McEntire, who seems to anchor the group, also serves as its main drummer/percussionist, though being a “band” is about the last thing on Tortoise’s agenda. “It was just this collection of people,” he told The Wire in 1996. “Along with that, the instruments that most of us were proficient with didn’t necessarily include playing the guitar or singing. So we decided: why bother with that?”

podcast.title: Canadian Scene
podcast.body: A small but globally defining post-rock scene emerged in Canada, with bands like Do Make Say Think in Toronto (1995) and Godspeed You! Black Emperor in Montreal (1994), characterized by instrumental music, distorted guitars, diverse instrumentation, and political themes. "And that scene, small as it was, helped define post-rock for the entire planet."

podcast.title: Catalyst from Spiderland
podcast.body: Slint's *Spiderland* is recognized as the main catalyst for the post-rock genre, with its impact extending through word-of-mouth over the years to become a fundamental pillar of 90s music. "Spiderland será considerado el catalizador principal del género por rock."

podcast.title: Characteristics
podcast.body: Post rock is characterized by non-traditional song structures, importance of texture and atmospherics, unusual subject matter, and the experimental, unconventional use of rock instruments, often without typical riffs. This type of music would historically not have been played on the radio. "Song structure is definitely non-traditional. Texture is important. Atmospheric are paramount. And the subject matter is unusual."

srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Chicago School of Post-Rock
podcast.body: This distinct school focused on instrumentation, tight performances, clean recordings, and the use of instruments such as Fender Rhodes, electro-pianos, marimbas, and vibraphones, representing music that required rock to have existed for its own development. "The focus here was on instrumentation, type performances, clean recordings, and use of things like fender roads, electro pianos, marimba's, and vibraphones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Core Characteristics
podcast.body: It is rock music focused on experimentation, unusual uses of traditional rock instruments, an emphasis on texture and atmospherics, wide dynamic range, attention to repetition of musical motifs, often completely instrumental, and cinematic in scope and nature. "To review, it's rock music that focuses on experimentation, unusual uses of traditional rock instruments, a focus on texture and atmospherics, lots of dynamic range, attention to repetition of musical motifs, and often, but not always, completely instrumental and very cinematic in scope and nature."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Definition and Implication of "Post"
podcast.body: The term "post rock" is baffling because the prefix "post" implies that this music comes after rock, suggesting rock is finished, yet rock is still very much present. It describes music that is different enough from "normal" rock to stand apart. "The use of the prefix post implies that this music comes after rock. Rock is over done finished and this is what comes next."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Definition and Philosophy
podcast.body: Post-rock implies music that comes "after rock," but since rock is still present, it is better understood not as a genre or a sound, but as a philosophy or aesthetic. It explores "what happens if rock instruments stop behaving like rock instruments," focusing on experimentation, unusual uses of traditional rock instruments, texture, atmospherics, dynamic range, repetition of musical motifs, and often instrumental or cinematic scope. "This term implies that there is already something that comes after rock. But rock is still very much with us, so what's so post about it? This requires a substantial amount of deconstruction, and this is part two of our attempt to define post-rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Early Usage of the Term
podcast.body: The term "post rock" dates back to 1967, appearing in a Time Magazine article about The Beatles' "Sargent Pepper" album, but it was popularized later by music writer Simon Reynolds. "The term had been around since, get this, 1967 in a Time Magazine article about the Beatles greatly forward with the Sargent Pepper album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Enduring Nature
podcast.body: Post-rock shows no signs of abating, continuously exploring new areas and sounds, with its experiments often trickling down to influence the broader rock world. "One thing is for sure though, post-rock shows no sign of a baiting. There are always areas and sounds to explore, and some of those experiments will continue to trickle down to the rest of the rock world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Global Reach and Influence
podcast.body: The post-rock world is truly global, with artists from Canada, the U.S., the UK, Poland, Iceland, and Japan. Its influence extends to movie soundtracks, TV themes, and video game music. "And this world is truly global. Canada, the U.S., the UK, Poland, Iceland, Japan. It figures into movie soundtracks, TV themes, video game music, and a whole lot more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Hybridization Potential
podcast.body: The genre lends itself well to hybridization with other forms of rock because it is largely instrumental and thus free of language barriers. "It does lend itself to much hybridization because it's largely instrumental free of language barriers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Instrumentation for Non-Rock Purposes
podcast.body: Simon Reynolds defined post-rock groups as "using rock instrumentation for non-rock purposes," such as employing guitars for texture and atmospherics rather than for riffing and power chords. "Groups that, and these are Simon Reynolds words, using rock instrumentation for non-rock purposes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Lyrical and Riff Emphasis
podcast.body: In post-rock, riffs are often secondary to texture, and while lyrics can be nice, they are not necessary, with the focus often on instrumentation to guide the listener on a wordless or nearly wordless musical journey. "Riffs, not smart about texture. Lyrics, nice but not necessary. Much of the time, the focus is on the instrumentation, and the goal is to take the listener on a wordless or nearly wordless musical trip."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Network and Global Reach
podcast.body: Post-rock functions as a network, spreading through word-of-mouth, touring, and platforms like Bandcamp, YouTube, and Discord. It is a global phenomenon, with artists from the US, Canada, UK, Japan, Scandinavia, Eastern Europe, China, Latin America, and Israel. "It's also a network. This music travels by word of mouth. It travels by touring and sites like Bandcamp and YouTube and Discord all play a big part."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Non-Traditional Outcomes
podcast.body: Despite using traditional rock instruments like guitars, bass, drums, keyboards, and outboard gear, post-rock produces non-rock outcomes, avoiding typical verse-chorus structures in favor of atmospheric, experimental, and cinematic compositions. "What we're doing is producing non-rock outcomes. That means compositions without the usual verse chorus, verse structure, and more atmospheric, some more experimentation, and more of a cinematic approach to audio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Recommended Bands for Exploration
podcast.body: To explore post-rock further, one can look into bands such as Talk Talk, Slint, Bark Psychosis, Tortoise, Mogwai, Stereolab, Godspeed You! Black Emperor, Sigur Rós, Explosions in the Sky, Mono, This Will Destroy You, God Is An Astronaut, and Russian Circles. "If you want to go deeper, look into bands like Talk Talk, Slint, Barxide Coses, Tortoise, Magwai, Stereolab, Godspeed you, Black Amper, we always keep coming back to them. Singer Rousse, Explosions in the Sky, Mono, this will destroy you, God is an astronaut and Russian circles."

podcast.title: Regional Approaches - Japan
podcast.body: The Japanese post-rock scene is largely characterized by precision in its musical execution. "We could also look to Japanese Post Rock. That scene is largely about precision."

srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Regional Approaches - Montreal/Chicago
podcast.body: Post-rock from Montreal and, to a certain extent, Chicago, is often more political and intellectual in its expression. "Montreal Post Rock, and to a certain extent, Chicago, is more political and intellectual."

podcast.title: Regional Approaches - Texas
podcast.body: Texas post-rock bands are distinguished as among the most cinematic in their musical approach. "And Texas Post Rock bands are among the most cinematic."

podcast.title: Regional Approaches - UK
podcast.body: Post-rock bands from the UK tend to be spacey while also exhibiting restraint in their music-making. "Bands from the UK tend to be rather spacey while at the same time exhibiting some restraint in their music making."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: Retrospective Application of the Term
podcast.body: Once "post rock" entered the music vernacular, people began to retrospectively identify earlier groups that met its criteria, including My Bloody Valentine, Cocteau Twins, early industrial music bands like Throbbing Gristle and Einstürzende Neubauten, and Talk Talk. "People began to look back to see if there were any other earlier groups who met this criterion. And yes, there were."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Simon Reynolds' Popularization
podcast.body: Music writer Simon Reynolds helped popularize the term "post rock" in the 1980s and first used it in print in 1993 to describe Bark Psychosis's album "Hex." "Reynolds helped popularize it in the 1980s. The first time he used an imprint was in 1993, when he was searching for a way to describe an album entitled Hex by a group called Barke Psychosis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post-Rock? Part 1

podcast.title: Structure and Dynamics
podcast.body: Post-rock often features long tracks that slowly and leisurely evolve, incorporating a wide dynamic range from whisper-quiet to overwhelmingly loud, frequently creating an emotional arc or oral narrative. "Long tracks that slowly and leisurely evolve with plenty of dynamics ranging from whisper-quiet to overwhelming loudness. Many pieces are wrapped in a sort of oral narrative that can be best described as an emotional arc."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2

podcast.title: UK Experimental Scene (Late 80s/Early 90s)
podcast.body: The UK harbored an experimental scene in the late 1980s and early 1990s that included bands like Talk Talk, Stereolab, Lika, Seefeel, Moonshake, and Disco Inferno, characterized by jazz-style rhythms, spacious production, atmospherics, and dynamics. "Talk Talk was part of an experimental scene in the UK through the late 80s and early 1990s."
